flagged.title: Thinking Like a Migration Historian
flagged.reason: The video presents an inaccurate exam paper structure, claiming 'Explain why' is an 8-mark question and that the Notting Hill section features a 12-mark essay, when 'Explain why' is 12 marks and Notting Hill has no essay.

mark_affecting.quote: Explain why for eight marks... From the Notting Hill section, you'll face a 12-mark essay.
Describe: Two precise features (4 marks)... Explain why: Two reasons developed (8 marks)

flagged.title: Normans, Jews and Medieval Traders, c1066–c1500
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly states that Henry III granted privileges to Hanseatic merchants in 1281 (Henry III died in 1272; Edward I was king and confirmed privileges in the Carta Mercatoria of 1303), which would penalise students for factual inaccuracy.

mark_affecting.quote: Granted special privileges by Henry the Third back in 1281, these Hanseatic merchants imported vital goods...
Granted special privileges by Henry the Third back in 1281...

flagged.title: Early Modern Arrivals, c1500–c1700
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly credits Charles II with welcoming the 1685 post-revocation wave of Huguenots through denization proclamations, when Charles II died in February 1685 before the revocation occurred.

mark_affecting.quote: Now to handle a wave of people this big, King Charles II used a clever legal tool called denization... Charles II actively pushed royal proclamations promising denization just to encourage these destitute yet highly skilled French refugees to settle down in England.

flagged.title: Industrial Britain: Irish, Empire and Refugees, c1700–c1900
flagged.reason: The video cites an untraceable 1894 anti-Italian riot in Manchester and anachronistic attacks on German bakers during spy scares, teaching false historical events that would lose marks if used as evidence in exam questions.

mark_affecting.quote: You had anti-Italian riots breaking out in Manchester in 1894, and German bakers were routinely attacked during national spy scares.

flagged.title: Case Study: Liverpool and the Irish in the 19th Century
flagged.reason: The video repeats the debunked claim that over 300,000 Irish received poor relief in 1846 alone and incorrectly states that Liverpool sent two Irish Nationalist MPs rather than one (T. P. O'Connor for Liverpool Scotland).

mark_affecting.quote: In 1846, over 300,000 Irish received poor relief, buckling the system.
Two Irish Nationalist MPs sent to Westminster.

flagged.title: Case Study: Jewish East End and the Aliens Act, c1880–1914
flagged.reason: The video states that the British Brothers' League was founded in 1902 by Major William Evans-Gordon, teaching the wrong founder and founding year instead of William Stanley Shaw in May 1901.

mark_affecting.quote: By 1902 we see a group called the British Brothers' League founded by a Conservative MP Major William Evans-Gordon.

flagged.title: Modern Britain: Wars, Empire's End and the Law, c1900–present
flagged.reason: The video states the outdated figure of 492 passengers for the Empire Windrush (F32), which teaches an inaccurate figure and contradicts the corrected lesson text and assessments.

flagged.title: Notting Hill: Riots, Racism and Policing
flagged.reason: The video actively teaches students incorrect exam evidence, citing an unverified police file (MEPO 2/9838) claiming it confirmed white-led violence, stating Mosley came third rather than fourth/last, and giving an incorrect prison sentence for the rioters.

mark_affecting.quote: sentencing nine white men to four years each
You can quote the Metropolitan Police file MEPO 2/9838... It officially confirms that the violence was largely white-led.
It meant he actually finished third, beating the Liberal candidate.

flagged.title: Notting Hill: Black Activism and the Mangrove
flagged.reason: The video states that the Metropolitan Police made a humiliating apology when historically there was no apology, and incorrectly claims only two of the Mangrove Nine were acquitted when five were acquitted on all charges.

mark_affecting.quote: Two were completely acquitted of all charges, and the rest received minor suspended sentences.
It forced the Met into a humiliating apology.
